correctness.rationale: Exact diagonalized residual identity yields a new uniform perpendicular direction every time; the logarithmic norm increments after startup are integrable and one-dependent, permitting an even/odd strong law. Two elementary logarithmic circle integrals supply the asserted Lyapunov exponent. Conditioning on a non-eigenvector residual, the ratio of independent Gaussian coordinates has infinite p-moment for p≥1; that remains true at every iteration. The symbolic program checks the update identity and corroborates the angular formula; finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The exactly computed Lyapunov exponent for independently resampled scalar test sketches and simultaneous divergence of all positive-time moments is not implied by the inspected sketched-GMRES analyses, previous Gaussian correction-direction minimization, deterministic optimal Richardson rate, or Gaussian Galerkin single-solve moment laws.
residual_risks: A conceptually equivalent result could be recorded under random Möbius products, randomly projected Richardson, or random hyperplane iterations in literature not inspected.
The same numerical rate is classical for optimally tuned deterministic Richardson, but equality of rates is not identity of algorithms; that coincidence alone is not presented as novelty.
The infinite-moment observation alone is implied by a Gaussian reciprocal pole and is not presented as a standalone new theorem.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural sharp underembedding question for sketched residual solvers: unexpectedly, the worst possible first-and-higher residual moments coexist with the exact stable optimal Richardson pathwise rate in the definite planar case. It exposes a concrete mismatch between mean-risk and typical convergence outside the subspace-embedding regime, with a structural proof rather than one numerical example.
